judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The link text is "aqui" (href #Editais), but the live HTML and the snapshot show its enclosing sentence, in the same text block: "Acompanhe aqui as publicações do vestibular FUVEST 2027." Link text plus its programmatically determined sentence context gives the purpose (the vestibular's publications). That is sufficient technique G53, so 2.4.4 (Level A) passes; only 2.4.9 (AAA) would require a self-describing link. The sentence was in the packet's ancestor text, so the model misjudged.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'next page' link of the Últimas Notícias pagination (nav aria-label="Pagination"). Its only text is "»", with no screen-reader text, title or aria-label. The live HTML shows Elementor gave the page-number links hidden 'Page' text but not this one. Screen readers announce the guillemet as a symbol name, or nothing at default punctuation levels, and no sentence, list or cell context says 'next page'. The purpose rests only on visual convention, so 2.4.4 fails. The finding's 'nothing around it does' is slightly overstated (the nav label hints at pagination), but the failure stands.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: An h2 "01/11/2026" in the exam-phases block. It is the date pill under '1ª FASE / MÚLTIPLA ESCOLHA', followed by '80 QUESTÕES' and the curricular components. In this exam schedule the date identifies the exam day whose content is described below, so it describes the topic. 2.4.6 only asks headings to describe topic or purpose, not to be exhaustive. Whether a date should be a heading at all is a 1.3.1 question, and the '1ª FASE' image with alt="" is a separate 1.1.1 issue. 'Data da prova: ...' would be a nicer label, not a fix for a failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The home link in the main menu (U+F015) has no aria-label, title or hidden text. Its name comes from its contents, which are only the private-use glyph U+F015: the snapshot's ax tree shows nameFrom contents, and the list item's name is \uf015. Minor inaccuracy: the glyph is literal DOM text styled with an icon font, not CSS-generated content, but the claim and the fix are right.
